title: The geopolitics of global hunger – European Council on Foreign Relations
gist: An ECFR podcast with Cary Fowler and Jim O'Brien on three converging shocks to global food supply — Russia's war disrupting grain exports, a blocked Strait of Hormuz restricting fertiliser shipments and a potentially severe El Niño — arriving at a moment when the 2022 cooperation mechanisms that averted catastrophe are far weaker.

insights.claim: Conflict, climate change and geopolitical fragmentation are converging into a growing risk of a global food crisis, with Russia's war disrupting grain exports, a blocked Strait of Hormuz restricting fertiliser shipments and a potentially severe El Niño threatening harvests across Africa, Asia and Latin America.
insights.so_what: Three independent shocks hitting the same commodity complex simultaneously — the correlated setup that produces price spikes rather than normal volatility in grains and fertiliser.
insights.locator: As conflict, climate change and geopolitical fragmentation converge
insights.speaker: Cary Fowler, Mark Leonard, Jim O’Brien

insights.claim: These overlapping pressures will hit hundreds of millions of people who are already food insecure.
insights.so_what: Sizes the humanitarian and political fallout, which drives migration pressure and import-demand policy responses in exposed states.
insights.locator: These overlapping pressures will impact hundreds of millions
insights.speaker: Cary Fowler, Mark Leonard, Jim O’Brien

insights.claim: Mechanisms to mitigate food insecurity exist — in 2022 the UN, the US, the EU and regional actors kept grain flowing from Ukraine and averted a broader catastrophe — but many of the conditions that enabled that cooperation are weaker today, creating a dangerous gap in global leadership.
insights.so_what: The 2022 playbook cannot simply be re-run, so the base case is a slower, worse-coordinated response than the last food shock.
insights.locator: While mechanisms are in place to mitigate the impact
insights.speaker: Cary Fowler, Mark Leonard, Jim O’Brien

insights.claim: Humanitarian ceasefires covering specifically grain exports and fertiliser shipments are the proposed practical mechanism, alongside treating food security as a central pillar of global security rather than a humanitarian side-issue.
insights.so_what: A narrowly scoped commodity ceasefire is the most tradeable de-escalation headline to watch in the Black Sea and Hormuz.
insights.locator: They discuss the roles of Europe, the UN and major powers
insights.speaker: Cary Fowler, Mark Leonard, Jim O’Brien

insights.claim: Any effective response depends on China, India and Russia as much as on Europe and the UN, raising the question of whether governments can overcome geopolitical rivalry to address a crisis no one wants.
insights.so_what: Identifies whose consent is actually required — European-led initiatives without Beijing and Delhi will not move physical flows.
insights.locator: They discuss the roles of Europe, the UN and major powers
insights.speaker: Cary Fowler, Mark Leonard, Jim O’Brien
